primitives.name: Performance Estimation
primitives.verbatim_quote: - **Phase 1 (performance estimation):** estimate each player's round performance as the unique zero of Q_i(p) = Σ_{j≻i} l_j(p) + Σ_{j∼i} d_j(p) + Σ_{j≺i} v_j(p) (Theorem 3.3), weighting wins/losses/ties by opponent-strength functions.
primitives.latex: Q_i(p) = \sum_{j\succ i} l_j(p) + \sum_{j\sim i} d_j(p) + \sum_{j\prec i} v_j(p)
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'Q_i(p)': 'Performance residual function, dimensionless', 'l_j(p)': 'Win-weighted opponent strength function, dimensionless', 'd_j(p)': 'Draw-weighted opponent strength function, dimensionless', 'v_j(p)': 'Loss-weighted opponent strength function, dimensionless'}
primitives.assumptions: Players' performance is modeled as a deterministic function of opponent strength and match outcome.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When opponent strength functions become non-monotonic or singular.

layer2.mapping: Maps match outcomes to latent performance scores via logistic regression with opponent-weighted residuals.
layer2.telemetry: Pair inversion rate and rank deviation.

primitives.name: Belief Update
primitives.verbatim_quote: - **Phase 2 (belief update):** MAP of posterior ∝ Gaussian prior × per-round logistic factors, i.e., minimize L(s) = L_2((s-p_0)/β_0) + Σ_k L_R((s-p_k)/β_k), L_2(x) = x2/2, L_R(x) = 2 ln(cosh(πx/√12)).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'L(s)': 'Objective function, dimensionless', 's': 'Player skill estimate, skill units', 'p_0': 'Prior performance estimate, skill units', 'β_0': 'Prior precision, skill⁻¹', 'p_k': 'Round performance estimate, skill units', 'β_k': 'Round precision, skill⁻¹'}
primitives.assumptions: Posterior is approximated by a Gaussian distribution with logistic likelihoods.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When logistic factors fail to converge or precision becomes degenerate.

layer2.mapping: Minimizes a composite loss combining Gaussian prior and logistic likelihoods to compute skill estimates.

primitives.name: Skill Evolution
primitives.verbatim_quote: - **Skill evolution:** Elo-MMR(ρ) pseudodiffusion — continuous transfer/decay of factor weights with κ = (1 + γ_t2/σ_{t-1}2)^{-1}, w_0^new = κw_0 + (κ-κ^{1+ρ})Σw_k, w_k^new = κ^{1+ρ}w_k.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'κ': 'Decay coefficient, dimensionless', 'γ_t': 'Skill drift rate, skill²·time⁻¹', 'σ_{t-1}': 'Previous uncertainty, skill', 'ρ': 'Evolution exponent, dimensionless', 'w_k': 'Weight for round k, dimensionless'}
primitives.assumptions: Skill evolves continuously via weighted diffusion of past performance.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When skill drift dominates or weights collapse to zero.

layer2.mapping: Models skill decay and transfer through time-varying weight kernels.

Elo-MMR constructs a Bayesian approximation to TrueSkill by treating performance as observed in the infinite-player limit, enabling efficient computation. Performance estimation (Q_i(p)) maps match outcomes to latent skill scores using opponent-weighted residuals. Belief update minimizes a composite loss combining Gaussian priors and logistic likelihoods, yielding robust skill estimates. Skill evolution models continuous drift and decay through pseudodiffusion of weights. The system avoids overfitting through adaptive subsampling and history compression. Failure modes include numerical instability in extreme performance regimes or breakdown of monotonicity in opponent strength functions.
